Focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography showed that, within the templated series, the macropore fraction of the reconstructed 5 µm × 5 µm × 5 µm volumes generally increased from 0.24 (AKD 1 wt%) to 0.77 (AKD 5 wt%), with apparently through-connected macropores in the most porous support, information complementary to N2 sorption. The actual Pt loadings (ICP-MS) were 2.25, 2.09, 1.31, and 1.25 wt% for AKD 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt%, with Pt nanoparticles of about 1-3 nm (TEM). In methylcyclohexane (MCH) dehydrogenation under an H2-rich feed, the reaction was far from equilibrium at 598-623 K, where the per-gram rates decreased in the order AKD 3 > 1 ≥ 0 > 5 wt%; at 623 K the rates per gram of Pt were 1.4-2.1 times higher on the AKD 3 and 5 wt% supports than on the template-free support. Intraparticle diffusion is most likely insignificant for the powder catalysts (Weisz-Prater), and the most macroporous catalyst was less active per Pt than the AKD 3 wt% catalyst at a similar Pt surface density, so the activity differences are associated with the Pt phase rather than with the macropores. A reversible plug-flow analysis gave the same activation energy for all catalysts over 573-623 K (30-32 kJ mol-1). The apparent activation energies (25.7-34.8 kJ mol-1, 523-623 K) were lower than that of a Pt/Al2O3 reference measured with the same apparatus and procedure (58.6 kJ mol-1, 523-598 K); this is a comparison of apparent values, both affected by the approach to equilibrium. As an order-of-magnitude projection that depends on the assumed diffusivity enhancement (3-30-fold), a first-order-equivalent Thiele analysis indicates that such a macropore network would raise the effectiveness factor of millimetre-scale pellets by about 1.6-4.8 times (2.6-3 times for a tenfold enhancement).

43038110.resumo:
Acute and chronic joint pain is the hallmark of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection, often progressing to debilitating persistent joint pain. No approved antiviral therapy is available. We evaluated the clinical and virological efficacy of early ivermectin administration in acute CHIKV infection.
This open-label, randomized trial enrolled and randomized 127 adult patients with acute chikungunya within 72 hours of symptom onset in Thailand. Patients were assigned (1:1) to oral ivermectin (400 µg/kg/day for 3 days) plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Before the 1-month endpoint, 7 patients were lost to follow-up, leaving a finalized complete-case cohort of 120 participants (n = 60 per arm) for primary efficacy analysis. Co-primary outcomes were time to acute joint pain clearance and the proportion of patients with persistent joint pain at 1 month.
Early ivermectin significantly accelerated acute joint pain resolution compared to controls (median 3.5 days [IQR 2, 6] vs 12.0 days [IQR 8, 35]; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 3.65, 95% CI 2.28, 5.84; p < 0.0001). Ivermectin was associated with a 92% reduction in the odds of persistent joint pain at 1 month (6.6% vs 30%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.08, 95% CI 0.03, 0.21; p < 0.0001). It also shortened fever clearance (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days; p < 0.0001) and accelerated viral clearance by day 7.
Early ivermectin intervention within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly accelerates clinical recovery, suppresses viral replication, and profoundly reduces persistent joint pain at 1 month. These findings position ivermectin as a promising, scalable therapeutic strategy against CHIKV.

43041397.resumo: The emergence and spread of Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistant parasites remain a significant hurdle to malaria control and elimination. However, how changes in transmission affect the evolution of drug resistance remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatiotemporal prevalence of drug resistance across three distinct eco-epidemiological zones of Ghana (Guinea Savannah, Forest and Coastal) by characterizing genetic polymorphisms in five drug resistance genes (pfdhfr, pfdhps, pfmdr1, pfk13 and pfmdr2). A total of 764 P. falciparum isolates collected between 2010 and 2017 were analyzed using amplicon sequencing. The artemether lumefantrine (AL) resistance-associated genotypes, pfmdr1-N86 and pfmdr1-N86 F 184D1246, were near fixation in the Forest zone (90-100% and 63.9-100%, respectively). The prevalence of pfmdr1-N86 also increased significantly over time in the Guinea Savannah and Coastal zones (χ2 = 7.13, P<0.05; χ2 = 7.19, P<0.05). Regarding artemisinin (ART) resistance, none of the validated Southeast Asian pfk13 mutations were detected. We also characterized mutations in pfmdr2, another ART resistance-associated gene, for the first time in the Savannah and Forest zones of Ghana. For sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) resistance, the resistance-conferring alleles pfdhps - 540E and pfdhps - 581G occurred at prevalences below 5% and 10%, respectively. Similarly, the pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540 haplotype, associated with full SP resistance, was detected in fewer than 5% of parasites. The observed resurgence of parasites carrying the chloroquine (CQ)-sensitive proxy marker pfmdr1-N86, together with the increase in CQ-wildtype marker (pfcrt-K76) prevalence reported in other studies, suggests that CQ sensitivity is re-emerging and may inform future consideration of CQ-based combination therapies. Additionally, the rarity of the pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540 and pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540G581 haplotypes, driven by the low prevalence of pfdhps - 540E and pfdhps - 581G alleles, supports the continued use of SP for preventive therapy in Ghana.

43042358.resumo: Bacteria are constantly challenged by rapid environmental changes and therefore require efficient acclimation strategies for survival. One conserved strategy is the stringent response, which is mainly executed when bacteria face nutrient limitation. Under those conditions, bacteria synthesize the signalling molecules pppGpp and ppGpp, which induce a metabolic adaptation program that regulates multiple cellular processes. While the importance of (p)ppGpp accumulation for stress adaptation is well established, their basal levels are also essential for coordinating metabolism and survival under non-stress conditions. However, how these basal levels are maintained when sufficient nutrients are available is largely unknown. In the current study, we demonstrate that ribosome binding of the (p)ppGpp synthetase RelA is compromised in the absence of the ATPase YchF, which was previously linked to stress response and polyphosphate metabolism. We furthermore show that basal (p)ppGpp levels are reduced in the absence of YchF and that amino acid derivatives, such as serine hydroxamate, inhibit growth of both the ΔychF and ΔrelA strains. However, under minimal-medium conditions or mild amino acid starvation, the ΔychF strain exhibits a more pronounced growth defect than the ΔrelA strain. Biochemical assays reveal that YchF interacts directly with the pseudohydrolase- and TGS-domains of RelA, which potentially promotes RelA binding to the ribosome. In conclusion, our data suggest that YchF serves as a so far unknown regulator of alarmone production in E. coli.

43042837.resumo: Although phosphate is the thermodynamically stable and overwhelmingly abundant form of phosphorus in Nature, the modern phosphorus chemicals industry still relies heavily on white phosphorus (P4) as its central feedstock. In the thermal process, phosphate rock is reduced with coke and silica at temperatures around 1500 °C to produce P4, which is then converted to intermediates such as PCl3 before further conversion to value-added phosphorus compounds. This reaction sequence is effective, but involves the reduction of phosphate under high temperature, followed by additional redox and functionalization steps before many target phosphorus compounds are obtained. We therefore asked whether phosphate-derived feedstocks could be converted more directly into reduced phosphorus compounds, making the production of P4 as an intermediate unnecessary while retaining the synthetic flexibility needed for producing a large variety of phosphorus compounds. That question led to three areas of investigation. The first exploits the strong thermodynamic driving force of Si-O bond formation to achieve oxygen-abstraction reduction of phosphate-derived substrates. This led to the discovery of the bis(trichlorosilyl)phosphide anion,[P(SiCl3)2]-, a previously unknown P(-3) synthon that can now be accessed from trimetaphosphate, orthophosphate salts, and phosphoric acid. It can be further converted to value-added phosphorus compounds, such as phosphines, hexafluorophosphate, or phosphonium salts. Protonation of [P(SiCl3)2]- gives bis(trichlorosilyl)phosphine,HP(SiCl3)2, which undergoes selective radical hydrophosphination and gives synthetic access to primary phosphines, chlorophosphines, phosphinic acids, phosphonic acids, and phosphonium salts. The second strategy uses mechanochemistry to convert condensed phosphates directly to phosphite through hydride phosphorylation. Ball milling with alkali-metal hydrides provides a solvent-free route to a P(III) product while retaining the PO3 framework of the starting material. This route also works with biologically recovered polyphosphate feedstocks, which is important for the recycling of sewage sludge. The same mechanochemical platform further proved useful for the analogous redox-neutral phosphorylation of acetylides, giving alkynyl phosphonates directly from condensed phosphates. Finally, strongly reducing mechanochemical conditions based on supported alkali-metal dispersions gave access to ortho-phosphite,PO33-, a previously "missing" phosphorus oxoanion. This new anion can be converted further to phosphite salts, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and alkyl phosphonates. Taken together, these studies show that condensed phosphates and phosphoric acid can be directly used as feedstocks for synthetic phosphorus chemistry, without relying on P4 as an intermediate. Complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria frequently presents with multiple life-threatening sequelae, including cerebral malaria, profound anaemia, and hyperparasitaemia. Although parasite densities exceeding 10% are independently associated with high mortality, achieving full recovery in a young child presenting with simultaneous extreme parasitaemia, deep coma, and severe malarial anaemia remains exceptionally noteworthy.

Laboratory investigations confirmed an extreme 14% P. falciparum parasitaemia and a life-threatening packed cell volume of 8%. 43038261.resumo: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. We introduce an innovative application of the Distillation of knowledge with NO labels v2 (DINOv2-l14) algorithm, a self-supervised learning (SSL) model, for the classification of 30 distinct mosquito species from image data. A key focus was enabling the model to learn effectively from a highly imbalanced dataset, where the number of images per class ranged from 15 to 124. We also investigated the data efficiency of SSL by determining the minimum data partition required to match the performance of a conventional supervised model. Our image processing pipeline involved cropping, padding, and dividing images into 14 × 14 patches before converting them into embedded vectors for classification. The fully trained DINOv2-l14 model significantly outperformed a selected ResNet101 baseline, achieving 99.2% accuracy, 97.7% specificity, an F1 score of 86.1%, and a robust area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.996. Most notably, when fine-tuned on just 20% of the available data (averaging 11-13 images per class), the SSL model achieved performance comparable to the baseline model trained on the entire dataset, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency. Although limitations exist, including dataset imbalance and a lack of standardization for broader application, the model's high performance across five-fold cross-validation and strong Cohen's Kappa coefficients (up to 0.836) confirm its reliability. This work validates a novel, efficient, and highly accurate AI-driven approach to mosquito identification. By integrating such a model into a mobile application using an embedding AI framework, this technology holds significant promise for empowering field personnel with a practical, powerful tool to enhance vector surveillance and control programs worldwide.

Hernias are a public health priority in Africa, with a focus on hernia surgery providing the potential to reduce the significant burden of hernia-related morbidity. Only a minority of patients in Africa are currently receiving a gold-standard mesh repair, owing to the cost of commercial mesh. In this study, we describe the long-term outcomes for patients undergoing hernia repairs utilising an affordable polyethylene 'mosquito-net' mesh (MNM) in Muheza, Tanzania.

Operative technique using a tension-free sublay technique and postoperative care, where feasible, was standardised. Follow-up was performed through a mix of face-to-face and telephone consultation.

Thirty-day morbidity rate was 3.5%, including one (0.4%) mesh infection and two patients (0.7%) who required a return to theatre. Chronic pain was reported in 17 (6.3%) patients. There was one hernia recurrence during the study period.
Following our reporting of the early results in 2020, we now offer the longer-term data to demonstrate that the Muheza Approach to hernias utilising MNM is a safe, effective, affordable and sustainable strategy that could provide a platform for wider implementation across LMICs to address the shortfall in high-quality hernia surgery.

Mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation are implicated in obesity-associated metabolic disorders. Studies interrogating muscle mitochondrial bioenergetics in obesity are confounded by the impact of age and/or physical activity. How obesity impacts mitochondrial bioenergetics in monocytes-precursors to muscle-resident macrophages-is poorly understood. We aimed to compare whole-body immunometabolic function and mitochondrial respiration in muscle and monocytes in adults with or without obesity of similar sex, age and physical activity levels.
In this cross-sectional study, young adults with obesity (BMI ≥ 30) or without obesity (BMI < 30) of similar age, sex and activity levels provided a fasted blood sample and muscle biopsy (vastus lateralis), and underwent a mixed-meal tolerance test. Mitochondrial respiration was measured in permeabilised muscle fibres and blood monocytes using high-resolution respirometry alongside muscle mitochondrial proteins and enzyme activity. Blood monocyte phenotype, polarisation and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) were quantified using flow cytometry.
Young adults with obesity (n = 17 [9 female/8 male], age 23.1 [SD 5.7] years, BMI 33.2 [SD 3.1] kg/m2) exhibited impaired whole-body insulin sensitivity (d = 1.2) and elevated white blood cell counts (d = 0.9; both p < 0.01) compared with those without obesity (n = 20 [10 female/10 male], age 22.8 [SD 4.6] years, BMI 21.8 [SD 2.1] kg/m2). Muscle oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS; d = 0.7-0.8) and electron transfer system capacity (ETS; d = 1.0) were higher in young adults with obesity than in those without obesity (p < 0.05) despite similar mitochondrial content markers (d = 0.2; p > 0.6). Monocyte OXPHOS (d = 1.0) and ETS (d = 0.8) were attenuated in those with obesity and accompanied by lower Toll-like receptor 4 expression (d = 0.7-0.8), diminished cytokine-stimulated mtROS production (d = 0.8-1.0) (all p < 0.05) and exaggerated proinflammatory marker expression ex vivo (d = 0.8; p = 0.07).
Young adults with obesity exhibit elevated muscle mitochondrial respiration-consistent with early adaptive remodelling in response to energy surplus-accompanied by heightened systemic inflammation and cellular markers suggestive of a dysregulated immunometabolic phenotype.

MCC-4 showed similar mitochondrial activating effects as MCC-2 but was devoid of any antibacterial or immune enhancing activity.
MCC-2 demonstrates promise for further development as an adjunct candidate to antibiotic therapy given its immunometabolic action in enhancing macrophage antimicrobial function while restoring mitochondrial competence through the putative target, 67LR.

Our findings establish a single transcription factor isoform as the smallest unit required to differentiate neuronal identity, a strategy that may be conserved within developmental programs to expand the capacity for cell-type diversity across animal species.

In vertebrates, adenosine accumulation resulting from adenosine triphosphate metabolization triggers sleep2. Specifically, size-related decreases of mitochondrial surface-to-volume-ratio might reduce the need for sleep by decreasing mitochondrial leakage of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We identify neural mitochondrial size as a possible cellular determinant of sleep duration.

43038759.resumo: The development and structural variety of stomatal complexes in Trochodendron aralioides, a species with primitive vessels, were studied. Light, scanning and transmission electron microscopy were used. The stomata have large outer ledges which form stomatal cavities. The guard cells that develop through maternal cells division initially lie on a level with the subsidiary cells. Mutual arrangement of stomatal complex cells changes during their growth. The subsidiary cells of mature stomata lie under the stomata and contain large lipid inclusions, which occupy most of their volume. Four generations of stomata were identified. The epidermis is dominated by tertiary and quaternary stomata. They are smaller than the primary and secondary ones and have the narrowest outer ledge apertures. Based upon the notion that the cavities with narrow apertures are able to decrease stomatal conductance and transpiration rate, and large lipid inclusions hinder hydropassive opening of stomata, it was supposed that these structures could be important for the evolution of some plants, i.e., that they could protect their more vulnerable than tracheids primitive vessels from cavitation and thus provide the possibility of their further structure modifications. Besides, stomatal cavities could represent a structural advantage across varying environments. The cavities occur in plants both in humid environments, where they impede the physical blockage of stomatal pores by water, and in arid ones, where they limit water loss. So, stomatal cavities, even when they have appeared in humid environmental conditions, were adaptive for the arid ones, and vice versa. If they have emerged early in plant evolution, they could contribute to the expansion of flowering plants into different environments.

43037760.resumo: In this work, solid-phase extraction based on iron oxyhydroxide (FeOOH) nanoparticles were used to extract and pre-concentrate cadmium ions in a precise and sensitive manner. The sensitivity and accuracy of the developed method have increased compared to conventional flame atomic absorption spectrophotometry (FAAS). The improved method provides simple, economic and efficient procedure for the determination of cadmium ions. FeOOH nanoparticles were synthesized by using a hydrothermal route. The nano-sized structure of the FeOOH was as indicated by X-ray diffraction analysis and scanning electron microscopy. Numerous variables, including the medium's pH, the amount of sorbent, mixing type and time, the eluent concentration/volume were optimized using a univariate approach. Optimal conditions resulted in limits of detection and quantification of 0.24 and 0.79 μg/L, respectively. Real samples were obtained from two different lakes (Horseshoe Island, Antarctica) and recovery experiments were performed for the accuracy check. Recovery percentages were calculated using the matrix matching method and high percent recovery results between 85.3 and 113.5% demonstrated the applicability and accuracy of the developed method for cadmium determination in complex environmental matrices.

43041974.resumo: Monodisperse, spherical sub-micrometer particles with clean, smooth surfaces are key materials used as composite reinforcements, abrasives, and tribological additives, but remain synthetically challenging to produce. Pulsed laser melting in liquids (LML) is an environmentally friendly, emerging route for producing such particles. However, demonstrations have so far been limited to batch reactors, which are difficult to scale up to industrial production. Here, we extend laser melting in liquids to a continuous flat jet flow-through reactor in which boron carbide composite nanoparticles (B4CC) dispersed in ethanol are fed perpendicular to a nanosecond pulsed high-power ultraviolet laser beam; this is complemented by additional experiments employing pristine boron carbide. We elucidate how flow conditions and the application of modern high-repetition-rate lasers alter particle formation pathways. Characterization of B4CC, irradiated at fluences of 45-135 mJ·cm-2, by transmission electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering, evidences the formation of a bimodal size distribution of spherical particles with mean diameters of ≈50 and ≈100 nm, verifying the parallel occurrence of isochoric reshaping and an aggregation-melting-fusion mechanism. While the smaller particle size fraction formed in accordance with thermal equilibrium calculations, the second size mode, derived from a multistep aggregation-melt-fusion pathway, was significantly smaller than predicted. Systematic variation of the number of laser pulses per unit volume (PPV) from 1 to 16 by tuning the interpulse delay (τIP) from 1.4 to 0.1 ms revealed an initial increase of the mean diameter of the second mode with PPV, reaching maximum size at 4 PPV. Interestingly, at higher PPV, further particle growth is arrested, probably due to an interplay between low particle mass concentration and shorter τIP limiting the number of aggregation-melt-fusion steps, indicating kinetically controlled particle formation pathways. If the laser fluence is increased to 180 mJ·cm-2, laser fragmentation in liquid prevails, and small mass fractions of ultrasmall nanoparticles (approx. 2 nm) are formed, which constitutes the upper limit of the LML process window. Overall, at the example of the ultrahard material boron carbide, difficult to process by other methods into perfect spheres, kinetically controlled LML in a flat jet flow-through reactor gives access to nanostructures in a size range previously unattainable by laser processing, establishing the basis for upscaling production in liquid flow with matched laser pulse numbers.

43042231.resumo:
In patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), perihematomal edema (PHE) is a major driver of secondary brain injury, yet the temporal dynamics of circulating neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated biomarkers and their clinical relevance to PHE progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize their longitudinal dynamics and associations with PHE progression and clinical outcomes after sICH.
In this prospective cohort study, 200 patients with sICH (70 surgical and 130 non-surgical) and 50 healthy controls were enrolled, with serial peripheral blood samples collected at four predefined time points. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), and neutrophil elastase-DNA (NE-DNA) complexes were quantified. NET-associated neutrophil phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, with scanning electron microscopy for complementary ultrastructural assessment. PHE volume was quantified using 3D Slicer, and 90-day functional outcomes were assessed. In the non-surgical cohort, five regression algorithms were compared for exploratory estimation of peak PHE volume from baseline features using all 36 baseline variables within nested cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the best-performing model.
Circulating NET-associated biomarkers were markedly elevated in patients with sICH (all P < 0.001), with descriptive plots suggesting different temporal patterns in the surgical and non-surgical subgroups. SEM revealed NET-like extracellular ultrastructures in peripheral neutrophils. In the non-surgical cohort, PHEV was highest at T3 (3-5 days after onset) among the four scheduled assessments; baseline MPO-DNA was strongly correlated with peak PHE volume (ρ = 0.76, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Within the non-surgical cohort, exploratory machine-learning analysis identified CitH3, MPO-DNA, and hematoma volume as the top-ranked contributors to peak PHEV estimation. Higher baseline MPO-DNA was also independently associated with unfavorable 90-day functional outcome in this cohort.
Circulating NET-associated biomarkers showed temporal changes after sICH. In the non-surgical cohort, higher baseline MPO-DNA was associated with greater peak PHEV and unfavorable 90-day functional outcome. These findings point to a biological link that larger multicenter studies now need to confirm; the machine-learning findings remain exploratory and require external validation before clinical application.

43038208.resumo: This cohort profile paper describes the Siyakhula cohort, a prospective longitudinal study of mother-child dyads during the ante- and postpartum period. The cohort was established to investigate how in-utero and early postnatal environments altered by maternal HIV status influence infants' growth trajectories, cognitive development, immune development and function, irrespective of the infant's HIV status. Pregnant women aged ≥18 years with singleton pregnancies at <22 weeks' gestation (as per best obstetric estimate, including ultrasound), regardless of HIV status, were recruited from January 2018 to January 2021 and followed throughout pregnancy. After delivery, women were approached for continued enrolment in the postpartum arm, which followed the dyads for 24 months. A total of 315 pregnant women (152 living with HIV and 163 without HIV) were recruited. Routine (pregnancy-related clinical data, HIV status, anthropometry) and research-specific (socio-demographic information, body composition analysis, diet, vaginal swabs, bloods) were collected antepartum. Cord blood and placental samples were collected intrapartum, while breast milk, stool samples, and blood were collected postpartum. Infants had anthropometric measurements performed at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, as well as 6, 12 and 24 months. Neurodevelopmental assessments were conducted during later follow-up visits. Extensive clinical, immunological, metabolomic, nutritional, and developmental data, together with a large biorepository of maternal and infant biospecimens, have been established. This paper provides an overview of the cohort design, participant characteristics, available data and biospecimens, completed analyses, and future research opportunities. Future plans include developing immunometabolic signatures associated with optimal and suboptimal growth and neurodevelopment of infants in the first two years of life.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

Michael Levin e colaboradores provaram que a manipulação de potenciais de repouso de membrana (Vmem) e fluxo iônico governa diretamente a polarização funcional de macrófagos entre estados pró-inflamatórios e de cicatrização/tolerância.

grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Contactoma Celular & Comunicação Não-Vesicular de Organelas
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

Seu grupo demonstrou que redes bioelétricas funcionam como um 'software de alto nível' que define a morfologia anatômica, a regeneração de membros e o comportamento inflamatório, conseguindo induzir o crescimento de olhos funcionais em caudas de girinos ou reprogramar tecidos apenas alterando a condutância iônica local.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Optogenética Não-Invasiva em Insetos Vivos (Canais CsChrimson)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Controle óptico remoto de neurônios, enterócitos e células musculares em mosquitos livres e intactos, usando luz vermelha profunda (CsChrimson) que penetra a cutícula sem lesão térmica.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Por décadas, testar a função de um circuito neuropeptídico ou da motilidade intestinal de um mosquito exigia dissecção traumática, microinjeção de drogas ou silenciamento por RNAi sistêmico (que afeta o inseto por dias).

A criação de canais de rodopsina de canal ativados por luz vermelha (CsChrimson, desenvolvidos por Boyden, Levin e colaboradores) permitiu que pesquisadores ativem subpopulações neurais e células enteroendócrinas específicas com um simples flash de LED vermelho enquanto o inseto voa ou se alimenta em tempo real, sem qualquer agulha ou anestesia.
